title: Passwords holding unencoded sub-delimiters in connection URIs
summary: Connection URIs (AMQP, Redis) whose password contains RFC 3986 sub-delimiters (! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =) written without percent-encoding. Synthetic passwords.
rationale: Sub-delimiters are legal unencoded inside user-info, so a password such as one holding a semicolon, dollar sign or equals sign is still one password. Treating ; or & as the end of the secret, as in a query string or a shell command, cuts it short and leaves the tail exposed. The MongoDB manual is stricter than the RFC grammar (it lists $ as a character to encode); the two grammars differ and neither is wrong, so the fixtures stay in the AMQP and Redis forms where the unencoded form is within the grammar the source states.

expectation.rationale: The AMQP URI grammar and RFC 3986 allow sub-delimiters in the password, so the whole run is the password by documented grammar; reporting it, and covering the whole run, is project policy (as for the family). The Redis page documents the redis://user:password@host:port/dbnum form with user and password optional but does not itself list which characters may appear unencoded; that part rests on RFC 3986.

sources.supports: userinfo = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" ); sub-delims are ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =.
redis-cli accepts the URI pattern redis://user:password@host:port/dbnum; user, password and dbnum are optional.
The MongoDB manual lists $ among the characters to percent-encode, a stricter rule than the RFC user-info grammar (recorded as a difference, not a conflict).
sources.locator: section "Find Your Self-Hosted Deployment's Connection String"
